subject: Renewal amendment: co-term to Jan 1 + 3-yr ramp and billing options
messages:

Subject: Renewal amendment: initial draft for co-terming + ramp schedule

Hi Olivia / Maria,

Thanks again for the productive renewal discussion last week. Per our convo, attached is an initial draft renewal amendment that folds your existing subscription into a 3-year term with a staged capacity ramp (year-by-year committed capacity increases) and two pricing options (annual vs. multi-year discount). High-level:

- Co-term target: January 1 (aligns with your fiscal year)
- Ramp: Year 1 = 40% of target reserved throughput, Year 2 = 70% (cumulative), Year 3 = 100%
- Billing: Option A = annual invoices at list with annual true-up; Option B = 3-year pre-commit with 8% multi-year discount + quarterly invoicing
- Auto-renew: default on with annual opt-out window; can flip to manual renewal if you prefer

I've attached the PDF: Crestline_Renewal_Proposal_Q3-2026.pdf. This is intentionally conservative on year-1 to allow burst credits if you outpace the committed throughput.

Next steps: can you confirm co-terming to Jan 1 works for procurement? Also let me know if procurement needs us to move invoicing into Q4 to match budget cycles — we can accommodate with proration. If OK, I'll loop in Lauren (AM) and Rishi (billing) to finalize proration details and redline.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

- Auto-renew: procurement is generally wary of auto-enroll clauses. Can you provide language that defaults to opt-in rather than auto-renew, or at least a clear annual opt-out window?

Looping Maria from our advisor/tech procurement for any technical or contracting flags.

Hi Olivia / Maria — appreciate the quick feedback. Short answers inline and a concrete proposal below.

- Co-terming to Jan 1: confirmed, we will set the effective co-term date to 2027-01-01 with a proration plan that bills from the signature date to Jan 1 as a one-time transition adjustment. See attached v2 which includes a prorated charge example.
- Invoice timing/Q4: we can issue the first invoice in Q4 and set the effective term to Jan 1; the proration worksheet shows how the dollars map to fiscal quarters.
- Auto-renew language: we'll change to an annual auto-renew that is "opt-out" via written notice 60 days prior to renewal. If procurement prefers opt-in, we can make that change but it will affect pricing (opt-in -> no auto discount). Please confirm preference.
- SLA: we'll include our standard SLA appendix and can add a tighter latency credit ladder for core inference endpoints per your request.

Proposed commercial structure (two options):

Option A — Annual commitment (default)
- Year 1 commit: 40% of target reserved throughput (baseline)
- Year 2 commit: additional 30% (cumulative 70%)
- Year 3 commit: remaining 30% (cumulative 100%)
- Pricing: list rate with volume discounts applied at each threshold (yearly true-up)

Option B — 3-year pre-commit (preferred pricing)
- 3-year term with 8% off list for entire term
- Yearly ramp locked as above, invoiced quarterly; early ramp attainment triggers an earned credit applied to future invoices

We can also include a "staged capacity reserve" addendum: if Crestline needs immediate burst capacity above committed levels, we can allocate burst pool with metered overage pricing and discounted pass-through if you convert bursts into committed capacity within 90 days.

Next steps: Lauren — can you confirm the proration math and the one-time invoice path? Rishi — can you validate the 8% multi-year discount and whether we need finance approval for the early-ramp credit model?

Thanks,
Ben

Attachment: Crestline_Renewal_Proposal_Q3-2026-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 1.4MB)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal amendment: initial draft for co-terming + ramp schedule

Hi all — looping in the proration schedule and a proposed operationalization. Key points: 

- Co-term effective date: 2027-01-01.
- Transition invoice: any signed amendment executed before 2026-10-31 will receive an initial invoice billed in Q4 2026 for the prorated period (signature date -> 2026-12-31). The annual term then begins 2027-01-01.
- Proration approach: daily pro-rate, applied as a single invoice line; we can also shift to quarterly amortization on request. (See co-terming_proration_schedule.xlsx attached).
- Auto-renew: proposed language is default auto-renew with an annual 60-day opt-out window. If procurement requires opt-in only, we need to remove a 2% auto-renew discount and escalate pricing approval.
- Ramp credits: suggested mechanism — if Crestline exceeds a committed threshold in Year N by >=10% for two consecutive months, Redwood grants a one-time credit equal to 15% of the incremental monthly spend for that quarter, applied as a credit in the following invoice. (This is finance-approved for deals under $2M ACV.)

Rishi — finance has pre-approved the 8% multi-year discount and the early-ramp credit for deals under the threshold; for larger ACV we'll need a CFO exception.

Olivia — attaching the proration spreadsheet for your procurement/FP&A. If this matches your Q4 needs, Ben and I can prepare the final redline for signature.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
